The combination of emtricitabine, rilpivirine, and tenofovir disoproxil fumarate (TDF) is indicated as a complete regimen for the treatment of HIV-1 infection in treatment-naïve adults with HIV-1 RNA levels ≤100,000 copies/mL at the start of therapy. It is also indicated for certain virologically suppressed patients (HIV-1 RNA <50 copies/mL) who are on a stable antiretroviral therapy (ART) regimen. The recommended dose is one tablet (emtricitabine 200 mg/rilpivirine 25 mg/tenofovir 300 mg) taken orally once daily with a meal. 2. This combination is also approved for use in treatment-naïve adolescents aged 12 years or older who weigh at least 35 kg, with HIV-1 RNA levels ≤100,000 copies/mL, and in virologically suppressed patients on a stable ART regimen to replace their current ART. Safety and efficacy have not been established in children under 12 years of age. The recommended dose for adolescents is the same: one tablet taken orally once daily with a meal. 3. Carbamazepine decreases rilpivirine levels by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated, as it may lead to a loss of virologic response and potential resistance to rilpivirine or the NNRTI class. 4. Dexamethasone (systemic) decreases rilpivirine levels via CYP3A4 induction. Co-administration is contraindicated due to the risk of virologic failure and resistance. 5. Rilpivirine should not be co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inducers, as this can result in a loss of virologic response and potential resistance to rilpivirine or the NNRTI class. 6. Dexlansoprazole increases gastric pH, which decreases rilpivirine levels. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Co-administration is contraindicated, as it may lead to treatment failure and/or resistance to rilpivirine or NNRTIs. 7. Efavirenz decreases rilpivirine levels via CYP3A4 induction. Co-administration is contraindicated, as rilpivirine should not be used in combination with other NNRTIs. 8. Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir is a complete regimen for HIV and should not be co-administered with other antiretrovirals, including rilpivirine. Co-administration is contraindicated. 9. Eslicarbazepine acetate decreases rilpivirine levels via CYP3A4 induction. Co-administration is contraindicated due to the risk of virologic failure and resistance. 10. Esomeprazole increases gastric pH, reducing rilpivirine levels. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Co-administration is contraindicated, as it may lead to treatment failure and/or resistance. 11. Etravirine decreases rilpivirine levels via CYP3A4 induction. Co-administration is contraindicated, as rilpivirine should not be used in combination with other NNRTIs. 12. Co-administration is contraindicated, as it may lead to treatment failure and/or resistance. 14. Nevirapine decreases rilpivirine levels via CYP3A4 induction. Co-administration is contraindicated, as rilpivirine should not be used in combination with other NNRTIs. 15. Omeprazole increases gastric pH, reducing rilpivirine levels. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Co-administration is contraindicated, as it may lead to treatment failure and/or resistance. 16. Vonoprazan decreases rilpivirine levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. Co-administration is contraindicated. 25. Adagrasib and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval, increasing the risk of torsades de pointes and other serious arrhythmias. Co-administration should be avoided or alternative drugs should be used. If unavoidable, frequent ECG monitoring is recommended. 26. Amisulpride and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration should be avoided or alternative drugs should be used. ECG monitoring is recommended if co-administered. 27. Anagrelide and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration should be avoided or alternative drugs should be used. 28. Artemether and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration should be avoided or alternative drugs should be used. 29. Rilpivirine and atidarsagene autotemcel may interfere with each other. Antiretroviral therapy should be discontinued at least one month before cell mobilization and until all cycles of apheresis are completed. 30. Bedaquiline and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration should be avoided or alternative drugs should be used. 31. Rilpivirine and betibeglogene autotemcel may interfere with each other. Antiretroviral therapy should be discontinued at least one month before mobilization and until all apheresis cycles are completed. 32. Buprenorphine (all forms) and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration should be avoided or alternative drugs should be used. 33. Ceritinib and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration should be avoided or alternative drugs should be used. 34. Desflurane and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration should be avoided or alternative drugs should be used. 35. Dofetilide increases rilpivirine toxicity via QTc prolongation. Co-administration should be avoided or alternative drugs should be used. 36. Efavirenz and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration should be avoided or alternative drugs should be used. 37. Elivaldogene autotemcel and rilpivirine may interfere with each other. Antiretroviral therapy should be discontinued at least one month before stem cell mobilization and until all apheresis cycles are completed. 38. Co-administration should be avoided or alternative drugs should be used. 40. Eribulin and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration should be avoided or alternative drugs should be used. 41. Fexinidazole and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration should be avoided or alternative drugs should be used. Avoid combining fexinidazole with drugs that block potassium channels or prolong the QT interval. 42. Rilpivirine and givinostat both prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration should be avoided or alternative drugs should be used. If unavoidable, obtain ECGs at baseline, during concomitant use, and as clinically indicated. Withhold treatment if QTc >500 ms or if there is a >60 ms change from baseline. 43. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration should be avoided or alternative drugs should be used. 44. Isoflurane and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration should be avoided or alternative drugs should be used. 45. Lefamulin and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration should be avoided or alternative drugs should be used. 46. Rilpivirine and lovotibeglogene autotemcel may interfere with each other. Antiretroviral therapy should be discontinued at least one month before mobilization and until all apheresis cycles are completed. Some long-acting ARTs may require a longer discontinuation period. 47. Macimorelin and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration should be avoided or alternative drugs should be used. Macimorelin increases the QTc interval by ~11 ms. Allow sufficient washout time of QT-prolonging drugs before administering macimorelin. 48. Ombitasvir/paritaprevir/ritonavir & dasabuvir (DSC) increase rilpivirine levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Co-administration should be avoided or alternative drugs should be used. Concurrent use with rilpivirine is not recommended due to the risk of QT prolongation. 49. Oxaliplatin and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration should be avoided or alternative drugs should be used. 50. Ribociclib increases rilpivirine toxicity via QTc prolongation. Co-administration should be avoided or alternative drugs should be used. 51. Rifabutin decreases rilpivirine levels via CYP3A4 induction. If co-administered, increase rilpivirine dose to 50 mg once daily. When rifabutin is stopped, reduce rilpivirine dose to 25 mg once daily. 52. Sevoflurane and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration should be avoided or alternative drugs should be used. 53. Siponimod and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration should be avoided or alternative drugs should be used. 54. Tetrabenazine and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration should be avoided or alternative drugs should be used. 55. Tovorafenib decreases rilpivirine levels via CYP3A4 induction. Co-administration should be avoided or alternative drugs should be used. If unavoidable, monitor for loss of efficacy. 56. Rilpivirine increases toxicity of umeclidinium bromide/vilanterol inhaled via QTc prolongation. Co-administration should be avoided or alternative drugs should be used. Exercise caution when co-administering vilanterol with QT-prolonging drugs. 57. Rilpivirine increases toxicity of vilanterol/fluticasone furoate inhaled via QTc prolongation. Co-administration should be avoided or alternative drugs should be used. Exercise caution when co-administering vilanterol with QT-prolonging drugs. 58. Albuterol and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 59. Rilpivirine and alfuzosin both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 60. Aluminum hydroxide increases gastric pH, reducing rilpivirine levels. Co-administration may significantly decrease rilpivirine plasma concentrations. If antacids must be used, administer them at least 2 hours before or 4 hours after rilpivirine. For dolutegravir/rilpivirine combination products, administer antacids at least 4 hours before or 6 hours after. 61. Rilpivirine increases toxicity of amiodarone via QTc prolongation. Use caution and monitor closely. Co-administration with drugs that increase the risk of torsades de pointes should be approached cautiously. 62. Rilpivirine increases toxicity of amitriptyline via QTc prolongation. Use caution and monitor closely. Co-administration with drugs that increase the risk of torsades de pointes should be approached cautiously. 63. Rilpivirine increases toxicity of amoxapine via QTc prolongation. Use caution and monitor closely. Co-administration with drugs that increase the risk of torsades de pointes should be approached cautiously. 64. Rilpivirine increases toxicity of apomorphine via QTc prolongation. Use caution and monitor closely. Co-administration with drugs that increase the risk of torsades de pointes should be approached cautiously. 65. Arformoterol and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 66. Aripiprazole and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely.
